name: NeoTask
description: NeoTask is a pure-Python async task queue and scheduler: embedded by design, zero external services, with priorities, delayed, periodic and Cron tasks, checkpoint resume, cost tracking and lightweight monitoring, scaling to a distributed cluster through Redis.
author: NeoPen

releases.summary: Full-path performance fixes: prefetch empty-queue backoff, in-memory queue batch write/remove, blocking monitoring samples, and Redis batch reads.
items: Prefetch workers no longer add exponential backoff on an empty queue; sparse latency drops from up to 500 ms to 12–26 ms
In-memory batch push becomes O(k log n); pushing 1,000 items into a 10,000-item queue takes 0.471 ms
Batch remove uses lazy tombstones; removing 1,000 items takes 0.668 ms without rebuilding the heap
psutil sampling moves to a thread pool, removing periodic ~100 ms event-loop stalls
Redis list_by_status uses one MGET; memory pagination and Blackboard TTL writes optimized
Regression: 538 unit tests passed / 12 skipped; 87 integration tests passed / 1 skipped

releases.summary: Performance and lightweight monitoring: snapshots, periodic push, plus 1,000-task concurrency, checkpoint and progress benchmarks.
items: Added TaskPool.get_metrics() lightweight snapshot and on_metrics() periodic push
Added repository count and retry-count APIs so snapshots avoid loading task entities
Added 1,000-task concurrency, submit latency, and batch throughput benchmarks
Added checkpoint write cost and monitoring snapshot cost benchmarks
Added a benchmark for progress-report frequency impact on throughput
Unsubscribed events are no longer enqueued; internal handlers subscribe by event type
SQLite skips no-op commits in autocommit mode and prunes checkpoints only when over limit

releases.summary: Scheduling precision and executor configuration fixes.
items: Fixed scheduling precision for timed tasks
Fixed executor configuration not taking effect on some paths

releases.summary: Upgrade experience and stability: concurrent upgrades of existing databases, startup schema readiness, and metrics read races.
items: Idempotent column additions for old databases, fixing startup crashes from duplicate columns
Added TaskRepository.ensure_ready(), returning only after startup completes
Fixed deque iteration crashes during concurrent metrics reads
Relaxed the redis extra upper bound to <8 for redis-py 7.x

releases.summary: Local capability completion: checkpoint resume, business failures, cost and duration, parent/child tasks, and Blackboard.
items: Added CheckpointRepository for all three backends and resume paths
Added business failure reporting via report_failure() and the failure_reason field
Added cost tracking, queue_wait_ms / duration_ms and parent/child APIs
Added the memory-only Blackboard local context
Added task.checkpointed / task.cost_reported events and external task_id idempotency
Automatic column migration for old SQLite databases and a task_checkpoints table

releases.summary: Event-driven scheduling, EventBus backpressure and terminal cleanup; fixed pause deadlocks and SQLite commit races.
items: Prefetch and workers become event-driven; idle wakeup latency drops to about 1.3 ms
EventBus supports bounded queues, drop counts, and slow-handler warnings
Automatic terminal task cleanup and cleanup_terminal_tasks()
Added the neotask --benchmark lightweight benchmark entry point
Fixed submit deadlocks after pause and SQLite concurrent commit races
Redis heartbeat / reclaimer switches take effect; TaskPoolConfig.redis() enables Redis locks

releases.summary: Distributed-path fixes; dead-letter queue, timing wheel, and metrics wired in; dependencies reduced to aiosqlite + croniter.
items: Redis distributed locks renew per key, fixing cross-lock interference
Orphan reclaim filters by node, avoiding damage to other nodes
Explicit QueueFullError when the queue is full
Periodic missed policy: IGNORE / SKIP / RUN_ONCE / CATCH_UP
Dead-letter queue, timing wheel, and metrics connected to the main path
Exponential backoff for empty prefetch batches
Minimum Python 3.8
